answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a slashable stake before it earns rewards, with honest work slowly building a non-transferable reputation. A newcomer starts as a lone island with no trust, while a fake plume of identities must fund every clone and risks losing all stakes at once when correlated behavior triggers slashing. Even a whisper of collusion across clones can be detected by comparing their timing and counterparties, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply into many voices.
